newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian factions agree on rules for local polls.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian factions agree on rules for local polls.

text.p: Bosnia's Moslems, Serbs and Croats agreed on Tuesday with Western mediators on rules for voter registration in hotly-contested local elections scheduled for July.

"I am happy to announce that the Provisional Election Commission (PEC) adopted rules and regulations for voter registration," Robert Frowick, head of the Bosnian mission of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), told a news conference.

The OSCE mission is charged with supervising Bosnia's first local elections since the end of a 43-month war in November 1995. National polls were held in September which elected an inter-ethnic parliament and collective presidency.
Frowick said the rules were adopted by consensus among representatives of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation and Serb entity.
"Our firm target date (for voting) is July 12 and 13," he added.

It remained unclear whether the set of eight articles adopted on Tuesday would allay concerns that voting would recognise the results of wartime ethnic expulsions which displaced up to two million people.
Moslem, Croat and Serb nationalist political parties which dominate Bosnia view the local polls as a battle for control of territory which was fought over during the 1992-95 conflict.

The OSCE, which supervised the national voting in September, had to postpone municipal elections after Bosnian Serb authorities were accused of trying to legalise the results of "ethnic cleansing" by manipulating registration of refugees.
"Last year we extended a sort of a carte blanche and it was abused by state authorities," Frowick said. "This time we are determined to have stronger OSCE supervision."
Under the new rules Bosnians could opt to vote in their current municipality if they submitted proof they had settled there before July 31, 1996.
The agreement imposes stricter rules on refugees living abroad who wish to vote where they "intend" to live.

The refugees have to submit documents proving they had property, steady employment or owned a private business in the municipality. A letter of invitation from next of kin who live in the town would also suffice.
Frowick said the new rules would be strictly applied and violation of registration procedures could result in striking a candidate or a whole party from the election.
The national vote in September re-elected the same nationalist parties which were in power when fighting erupted in the former Yugoslav republic four years ago.
Opposition parties complained the elections were held without provisions for free press or proper supervision of voter registration and ballot counting.
